subject: Lendly: throughput collapse and hallucination rise post-quant-profile rollout
messages:
From: Tara Singh To: sergio_alvarez Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700 Subject: Realtime API: sudden p99 jump + hallucination increase after v4.2 qprofile Sergio — We started seeing a sharp p99 jump (from ~320ms to ~1.6s) and a ~2.4% uptick in hallucination flags for the Lendly ConfirmFlow model after your team rolled v4.2 with the new qprofile yesterday evening. Throughput dropped by roughly 35% too and error rate (502) increased during peak hours. This is affecting our loan-origination pipeline (request volume ~120 req/s during peak) and causing timeouts in downstream microservices. Our ops team captured traces and a short perf report (attached). Can you please escalate and let us know the rollback plan? We need either a mitigation or a timeline for fix — this is impacting our demo environment and a scheduled customer pilot Monday. Attachments: perf_report_2028-03-08.pdf, error-traces.log Tara Tara Singh Head of Integrations, Lendly T: +1 415-555-0182 --- From: sergio_alvarez To: Tara Singh Cc: grace_oconnor , stephanie_nguyen Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 15:18:00 -0700 Subject: Re: Realtime API: sudden p99 jump + hallucination increase after v4.2 qprofile Tara — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the traces. I'm escalating to the SRE and model ops teams now (cc'd). We will:
- Triage immediately and identify whether the qprofile or runtime change is responsible
- Run an automatic rollback to the prior qprofile (v4.1) in the canary pool within the hour if we confirm regression I'll send a status update within 30 minutes and a mitigation timeline. Apologies for the disruption — we know how critical low latency is for your flow. Sergio Alvarez Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai --- From: grace_oconnor To: sergio_alvarez , stephanie_nguyen Cc: marissa_cole Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 15:31:00 -07:00 Subject: Re: Realtime API: sudden p99 jump + hallucination increase after v4.2 qprofile Sergio / Stephanie — taking lead on incident. Initial read of the perf_report shows large GC stalls on the GPU host and a change in tokenization distribution post-deploy. Hypothesis: the new quantization profile increased memory working set, pushing more requests into fallback execution paths and causing serial decode stalls. Immediate actions I'm kicking off: - Trigger canary rollback of qprofile to v4.1 for Lendly lane (will not affect other customers) - Lock further qprofile promotions until postmortem - Collect full kv-cache and allocator traces from the affected GPU nodes (requested from infra) - Notify Lendly with expected mitigation ETA I attached the initial perf dump and a short checklist for runbook steps. Attachment: perf_report_2028-03-08.pdf Grace O'Connor Director, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference --- From: stephanie_nguyen To: grace_oconnor , sergio_alvarez Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00 Subject: Re: Realtime API: sudden p99 jump + hallucination increase after v4.2 qprofile Quick debugging notes from model ops: - We confirmed the Lendly canary saw a qprofile binary that enabled two-bytes-per-token kernel fallback for a subset of layers — that path wasn't exercised in our regression harness (90% coverage gap). - Telemetry shows elevated kernel-launch latency and ~12% more CUDA synchronizations on requests that hit the fallback path. - There's also evidence of reduced softmax numerical stability on aggressive quantization for stop-token prediction, which could explain the hallucination rise. Actions taken: - Canary rollback initiated at 16:00 PST for the Lendly lane (v4.1 qprofile restored). Monitoring now. - Rolling back is already showing p99 trending down; still watching for error-rate normalization. Attachments: error-traces.log I'll follow up with a narrowed RCA and recommended mitigations (tighter qprofile validation, additional kernel-path unit tests, and de-risking rollout gating). Stephanie Nguyen Principal Model Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference --- From: sergio_alvarez To: Tara Singh Cc: grace_oconnor , stephanie_nguyen , marissa_cole Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 16:22:00 -07:00 Subject: Re: Realtime API: sudden p99 jump + hallucination increase after v4.2 qprofile Tara — quick status: we rolled the qprofile back to v4.1 for your lane at ~16:00 PST. Early metrics show: - p99 reduced from ~1.6s to ~380ms over the next 20 minutes - Throughput recovering toward previous baseline (approx +30% from worst point) - Error-rate (502s) trending down but not fully recovered yet; infra is clearing soft-fail queues Next steps: - We will keep v4.1 for your lane until a controlled revalidation is complete (target: 72 hours) - Stephanie and Grace will deliver a short RCA and remediation plan by EOD tomorrow - I'll coordinate a customer credit/ops remediation note with Marissa if needed (cc'd) Apologies again — I'll stay on this thread until resolved. Please send any other traces if you see recurrence. Sergio --- From: marissa_cole To: sergio_alvarez , grace_oconnor , stephanie_nguyen Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -07:00 Subject: Re: Realtime API: sudden p99 jump + hallucination increase after v4.2 qprofile Thanks for the fast containment. A few leadership asks: 1) Please prioritize a customer-facing RCA and an ops mitigation note (clear TL;DR, root cause, and concrete remediation timeline). 2) Include a recommended credit / goodwill gesture for Lendly (propose 2 weeks of service credit or a one-time engineering credit to help with their pilot). 3) Schedule a postmortem with product, model-ops, infra, and sales by next Wednesday. I want a list of action items with owners and due dates. Also add INF-7789 to the postmortem and link the raw traces. We should treat this as a high-severity release regression and freeze qprofile promotions until mitigations are validated. Marissa Cole VP, Customer Success (covering Enterprise Accounts), Redwood Inference marissa.cole@redwood.ai ---
